# third_party/dragonfly

Our fork of [Dragonfly](https://github.com/df-mc/dragonfly) v0.11.6 (commit `51dd9c1`), MIT, used through `replace` in the root `go.mod`. The first commit here is the unmodified copy, so `git diff c105f71 -- third_party/dragonfly` shows everything we changed.

## What we changed and why

A player used to report to one concrete type, the Bedrock `*session.Session`. Overmind's Java players talk to the same game through their own front end, with no Bedrock connection, so a player now reports through an interface.

- `server/player/reporter.go` (new): `player.Reporter`, the methods `Player` calls on its client, plus `world.Viewer`. `*session.Session` implements it unchanged.
- `server/player/reporter_test.go` (new): a session is a Reporter, a player uses the Reporter it was given, and a player with none still uses `session.Nop`.
- `server/player/conf.go`: `Config.Session` is a `Reporter` (one line, and one unused import removed).
- `server/player/player.go`: the `s` field and the return of `session()` are `Reporter` (two lines). The 111 call sites and the `== session.Nop` checks are untouched.

`Reporter` is small in change, not in methods: it has 73 methods of its own because `Player` really does call that many.

- `server/player/player.go` `Move` (6 lines, plus the `maxMoveDelta` constant and its comment, 4 lines): a move longer than 32 blocks is refused and the client teleported back. Upstream, `checkOnGround` walks the box swept by the move, loading every chunk under it: one packet of 4096 blocks held the world for 11.8 s and grew the heap by 658 MB. Bedrock's input handler reaches this directly, so the guard is here and not in a front end. `server/player/move_test.go` covers it and that shorter moves do what they did. A refused move resets fall distance, as any teleport does.

- `server/conf.go` (`vanillaOnce`: 2 lines replaced by 5, plus the import and the variable with its comment, 10 added in all): vanilla recipes and creative items are registered once per process. Upstream registers them again for every server made, appending each time, so a test process that starts dozens of servers sent ever larger recipe and creative packets until Bedrock bots began to fail to join. A process running one server sees no difference. `server/vanilla_once_test.go` checks a second server adds no recipes.
- `server/player/player.go` `BreakDuration` (4 lines): exports the player's own break time, with its held item, effects, water and air, so the Java front end can tell when a client breaks a block at once.

- `server/session/listed.go` (new, Java batch A): `session.List` and `session.Unlist` put a player that has no Session (a Java player) in every Bedrock player's list, now and for sessions that join later, as Bedrock lists its own players. Upstream had no way to reach a session's player list from outside the package. Two upstream places use it: `session_list.go` `Add` sends the listed players to a new session (3 lines added), and `world.go` `ViewEntity` treats a listed player like one with a session (1 line added), so Bedrock keeps its row instead of adding and dropping it around `AddPlayer`. `Unlist` forgets the runtime IDs sessions gave the player, so it must run after the entity has left its world; Overmind calls it from the Java front end's leave hook. `SetListedSkin` gives a listed player's rows a new skin (taken out and put back, for every session and those joining later), which the hub calls on each Java skin change: a row carries its skin with `OverrideAppearance`, and a Bedrock client went on drawing a Java player in the stand-in it was listed with although `PlayerSkin` brought the fetched Mojang skin. Overmind's `TestJavaSkinReachesBedrock` (javafront) fails without it.

- `server/world/mcdb/db.go` `storeBlockEntities` and `server/session/chunk.go` `subChunkEntry` (3 lines each, Java batch B): a block entity whose data is nil is skipped instead of having its coordinates written into the nil map. Dragonfly's stand-in for a block it does not implement is a block entity with nil data, so setting one without NBT and then saving the chunk, or a Bedrock client asking for its sub-chunk, panicked the world. Overmind's `TestBlockEntityWithoutDataIsSafe` (javafront) covers both. The other two such loops in `session/chunk.go` run only with `subChunkRequests` off, which it is not, so they are left alone.

- `server/player/attack_rules.go` (new, Java batch B) and `server/player/player.go` `AttackEntity` (3 lines added, 1 changed): `player.AttackRules`. When the Reporter a player reports to implements it, it decides the damage of that player's attacks and whether they are critical, given Dragonfly's damage. Overmind's Java front end uses it for Java's attack cooldown and weapon damage (a player follows its own edition's combat rules); the Bedrock session does not implement it, so Bedrock is unchanged. `server/player/attack_rules_test.go` covers both.

- `server/entity/action.go`, `item_behaviour.go`, `projectile.go` (2 lines added, 2 changed, Java batch C): `PickedUpAction` carries `Count`, how many items were taken. Upstream viewers learn only who picked up, after the stack was already split, so Java's `collect` showed the whole stack when a full inventory took part of it. The Bedrock session ignores the field. Overmind's `TestPartialPickupShowsTheCountTaken` covers it.

- `server/conf.go` and `server/server.go` `createPlayer` (4 and 3 lines added, Java skins): `Config.JoinSkin`, when set, may replace the skin a Bedrock player joins with, before the session spawns and anyone is shown it. Upstream offers no hook there: a handler's `HandleSkinChange` covers only later changes, and the player list has gone out by the time `Accept` returns the player. Overmind's `skins.blockOddShapes` uses it; `TestBlockOddShapes` fails without it.

- `server/session/overmind_skin.go` (new) and `session.go`, `session_list.go` `sendSessionTo`, `world.go` `ViewEntity` and `ViewSkin`, `handler_player_skin.go` (16 lines added, 4 changed; Bedrock persona skins): Bedrock viewers, the player itself included, get a Bedrock player's skin as its client sent it. Upstream turns the login data into a `skin.Skin` and every packet back through `skinToProtocol`, which drops persona pieces, piece tints, skin colour, arm size, animation data, the cape ID, the premium flag and the geometry engine version, and makes up a new skin ID each time. A Character Creator skin without its pieces is drawn as a default skin, by other players and by its own player, whose list row overrides its appearance. The session now keeps the client's skin in its network form (from the login, then from each `PlayerSkin` it sends, with `Trusted` and `OverrideAppearance` true as upstream sets them) and sends it while the player still wears that skin; when something replaced it (a `JoinSkin` hook, a `HandleSkinChange` handler, as `skins.blockOddShapes` does) the upstream conversion is used. Java players' rows are unchanged. Overmind's `TestBedrockPersonaSkinRelayedAsSent` (javafront) fails without it.

- `server/session/player.go` `invByID` and `openedInventory` (26 lines added, 5 changed; Java batch C fix rounds 1 and 2): the session kept a container's inventory as its open window and gave it to item stack requests while the block at the opened position was still of the right kind, or, for a chest's `ContainerLevelEntity`, without looking at the block at all. A chest that paired or lost its pair while a Bedrock player had it open has a new inventory (`Chest.pair` and `unpair` clone both halves), and breaking the opened half of a double chest (a player's break runs the break handler then clears the block; an explosion, `block/explosion.go`, clears it first, then runs the handler) leaves the other half with a copy of its own, so taking from the old window duplicated items. `openedInventory` gives the window only while it is still the inventory of the block at the opened position (the ender chest's own for an ender chest), for chests, shulker boxes, barrels, brewing stands and furnaces; otherwise the container closes and the request is refused. Overmind's `TestBedrockChestWindowFollowsPairing` and `TestBedrockChestWindowOpenedHalfBroken` (broken and exploded) reproduce the dupes without it; `TestBedrockTakesFromChest` checks a chest left alone still works. The Java front end has the same check of its own.

- `server/server.go` `PlayerByName` and `PlayerByXUID` (2 lines each, race fixes): they take `pmu.RLock` as `Player`, `Players` and `PlayerCount` do. Upstream read the player map unlocked while joins and leaves wrote it, and a handle found that way had no happens-before with its creation on the listener goroutine (a second race, in `EntityHandle`, that the lock also fixes). `server/lookup_lock_test.go` reproduces it under `-race`.

- `server/world/entity.go` `EntityHandle.World` (a field, its accessor and 3 stores, 16 lines; race fixes): the world the entity is in, nil while it is in none or closed, read without the handle's lock. A world calls its viewers on its own goroutine, and the world a player has left keeps calling the player's viewer until it runs the loader's removal (queued by `Loader.ChangeWorld`); the Java front end drops those calls by checking that its player is still in the world it views. `e.w` is read under `e.cond.L`, which `execWorld` holds while it queues work on a world, so a viewer could not take it from a world's goroutine.

- `server/world/overmind_txguard.go` (new), `world.go` `handleTransactions` (1 line changed) and `entity_schedule.go` `runScheduled` (1 line added), merge fix: a world's transaction goroutine never dies silently. A callback that called `runtime.Goexit` (as `t.FailNow` or a testify `require` does from a test's world callback) ended the goroutine that runs all of the world's transactions: nothing was logged, its waiters were never woken, the world stopped ticking and `Server.Close` hung on the players in it. Now `runGuarded` logs it with its stack, releases the transaction's waiters (its task fails with `ErrTransactionExited`) and starts a new goroutine on the queue. A panic there is logged with its stack and re-raised, so it still stops the process. `overmind_txguard_test.go` `TestWorldSurvivesGoexitInTransaction` hangs without it.

- `server/cmd/output.go` `PrintMessage` (new method, 7 lines with its comment; /give): adds a message as it is, any `fmt.Stringer`. Upstream's `Print` and `Printf` make a string of it and `Printt` takes only a `chat.Translation`, so a source could not show its own form of a message. The Java front end shows /give's reply as Java's own translation through it; the Bedrock session sends its `String()`, as for any message.
- `server/cmd/argument.go` `parseTargets` `@p` (6 lines replaced by 4; /give): `@p` sorts the players by their own distance. Upstream sorted the players by a separate slice of distances that the sort did not move with them, so `@p` could pick any player. Overmind's `TestJavaOperatorGivesBedrock` gives with `@p` among three players (it can pass upstream by luck of the players' order, but not fail here).

### World ticks (stage 1)

The fork came forward from stage 1 Task 5 to Task 4c fix round 2, the first change Overmind needed inside Dragonfly.

- `server/world/tick.go`: a loader's random-tick and entity-tick reach is the world's tick range held at least two chunks under the loader's own chunk radius (`tickCentres`), with its own chunk always ticked. Before, every loader ticked the world's tick range whatever its view distance, so a client asking for a small view distance made ticks read, and generate, chunks it had not loaded. Entities now tick only within that reach, not in every viewed chunk.
- `server/world/tick.go`, `server/world/weather.go`: nothing past every loader's tick reach changes, as on Bedrock, where chunks past the simulation distance stay loaded but do not tick. Lightning strikes only ticked chunks (a bolt past reach would never tick, so never close). Scheduled ticks there stay queued (`scheduledTickQueue.tickIn`; `tick` keeps its old meaning for upstream tests) and neighbour updates wait while their chunk is loaded, so liquids, falling blocks and fire resume when a player comes near. `lightningChance` is a variable so tests can raise it (`export_test.go`). The dead `anyWithinDistance` is removed. Tested by `overmind_reach_test.go`.

  Left as they are, and why that is harmless: redstone propagates within one tick from a change in reach, through at most 15 blocks of wire, and explosions and entity drops start from entities, which tick only in reach. Either can leave an entity (lit TNT, an item) at most a chunk past reach, which is still inside view (the reach is held two chunks under it). It freezes there and resumes when a player comes near, as any entity that walks out of reach does; unlike a bolt, it closes on its own once ticked.

- `server/world/tick.go`: a chunk ticks (random and scheduled ticks, neighbour updates, entities, lightning) only when its eight neighbours are loaded too (`tickable`, `neighboursLoaded`), as in Java. The two-chunk margin above holds only once a loader's whole view has arrived; while a player walks into new ground the chunks just past the reach are still queued, and a tick at a ticked chunk's edge read them through `Tx.chunk`, which waits in `chunkRequest.doImmediate` behind every chunk queued before it (3.5 to 10 s stalls with 4 workers under load). A synchronous world still ticks every loaded chunk. Tested by `overmind_tick_test.go` `TestTickNeverWaitsForAChunkBeingMade`.

- `server/world/tick.go` `tickBlocksRandomly`: each sub chunk draws its own `RandomTickSpeed` positions, as in vanilla. Upstream drew one position a round and carried it up through the sub chunks until it hit a random ticker, so a block sharing its spot with a ticker in a lower sub chunk (a leaf 16 or 144 blocks above lava or grass) was reached only by a draw made right after that ticker: measured in internal/app `TestLeavesDecay`, such leaves ticked about 20 times less often, and the last tenth of a cut tree's leaves took 30 s or more to decay. Tested by `overmind_tick_test.go` `TestRandomTicksReachBlocksAboveOtherTickers`.

- `server/block/leaves.go`: a leaf stays while a log is within 6 steps through leaves (`leafLogReach`, Java's rule; was 4). Overmind generates Java's trees, whose leaves reach 6 steps, so at 4 any change beside an untouched tree decayed its outer leaves. (Task W made this Java-only: see "World mechanics parity".) A leaf that finds its log clears its mark without a block update (upstream sent one, which marked its neighbours again for ever, so every leaf of a canopy searched on every random tick; at reach 6 that slowed ticks to 18 a second in `TestGenerationDoesNotStallTicks`). Tested by internal/app `TestLeavesDecay` and that stall test.

- `server/session/handler_request_chunk_radius.go`: a client's radius is held to at least 2 (`minChunkRadius`, `clampChunkRadius`), the smallest tick reach (0, the player's own chunk) plus 2, so a tick never reads an unloaded chunk. Tested by `overmind_radius_test.go`.

### World mechanics parity (stage 2, Task W)

The world's shared mechanics follow Bedrock, or Java under Overmind's Overjava profile; `internal/worldrules` holds the values and `internal/app` sets them per world.

- `server/world/overmind_mechanics.go` (new) "Overmind fork": `World.RandomTickSpeed` reports the world's speed, after its default. Overmind sets Bedrock's 1 or Java's 3 through `Config.RandomTickSpeed`, which already existed; internal/app `TestRandomTickSpeedFollowsProfile` reads it back.
- Leaf decay by edition. `world.Mechanics` (new, in `overmind_mechanics.go`; a field of `world.Config` and of `server.Config`, passed on in `server.go` `createWorld`, 1 line each) has `JavaLeafDecay`. Java's (Overjava): a leaf stays within 6 steps of a log, and any change beside it marks it (as before). Bedrock's, the zero value: 4 steps, face to face through leaves, and only removing a log marks the leaves in the 9 x 9 x 9 cube around it, or removing a leaf the 3 x 3 x 3 cube; nothing else marks a leaf. Bedrock's own generated trees put leaves up to 7 steps from a log and Bedrock keeps them, because nothing marks them. Measured on a Bedrock Dedicated Server 1.26.60 (Task W report). Changes: `block/leaves.go` (`leafLogReach` is a function of the world's mechanics; `NeighbourUpdateTick` marks only under Java's rule; 9 lines), `block/overmind_leaf_marks.go` (new: `Replaced` on `Log`, `Wood` and `Leaves`), and `world/world.go` `setBlock` (4 lines): a block that implements the new `world.Replacer` hears that it was replaced, after a `SetBlock` that sends block updates; the old runtime ID is read whenever block updates are on. Tested by `block/overmind_leaves_test.go` (each Bedrock case repeats a BDS measurement) and internal/app `TestLeavesDecay` (Overjava) and `TestLeavesDecayBedrock`.
- Nether lava: 7 blocks, one every 10 game ticks, as on both editions (minecraft.wiki "Lava", oldid 3870569); upstream ran it 3 blocks every 5. `world/dimension.go` (1 line: `time.Second / 2`) and `block/liquid.go` (`spreadDecay`, new, and its 5 callers that read `b.SpreadDecay()`): lava in the Nether loses 1 depth a block instead of 2. Tested by `block/overmind_lava_test.go`, with the Overworld and End unchanged (3 blocks, 30 ticks).
- Weather check of a chunk tick (both editions, minecraft.wiki "Tick" oldid 3868751): each ticked chunk of a dimension with weather has a 1 in 16 chance a tick to check one column (`world/overmind_weather.go`, new, called from `tick.go`, 1 line; `precipitationChance` set by tests through `export_test.go`). What it does is the block package's (`block/overmind_weather.go`, new, registered with `world.RegisterPrecipitation`): water on top of its column freezes where the temperature is under 0.15 and block light under 10, beside a block that is not water; snow falls where it snows and block light is under 10, a layer at a time. `world.Mechanics.JavaWeather` (Overjava) lays one layer at most and counts waterlogged neighbours as water; Bedrock builds a biome's own height (its snow accumulation's upper value times 8: 1, 2, 4 or 8 layers, ice spikes' 12 held to 8; "Biome" oldid 3878263) and lets waterlogged neighbours freeze water ("Ice" oldid 3877975). `block/overmind_snow_layer.go` (new): `SnowLayer` with all eight heights; it replaces worldgen's own one-layer type, which is now an alias of it. `world/world.go` `temperature` (3 lines): above Y 80 the temperature drops 0.05 every 40 blocks ("Biome" oldid 3878263, and Bedrock's own, study notes S4) instead of upstream's 1/600 a block above Y 64; the small height noise both editions add is left out. Tested by `world/overmind_weather_test.go`. No cauldron exists in the fork, so nothing fills with rain or snow; snow layers do not melt.

In all, in existing upstream files: the Java and race work 100 lines added and 14 removed, the transaction guard 2 added and 1 removed, the persona skin work 16 and 4, the tick work (`world/tick.go` 143 and 58, `world/weather.go` 13 and 4, `block/leaves.go` 11 and 3, `session/handler_request_chunk_radius.go` 12 and 3) 179 added and 68 removed, the /give work (`cmd/output.go` 7 and 0, `cmd/argument.go` 4 and 6) 11 added and 6 removed, 308 added and 93 removed together. The rest is in new files (`reporter.go` 105, `reporter_test.go` 48, `move_test.go` 60, `vanilla_once_test.go`, `session/listed.go` 113, `playerdb/snapshot.go` 33, `player/attack_rules.go` 24, `player/attack_rules_test.go`, `lookup_lock_test.go`, `world/overmind_reach_test.go` 204, `world/overmind_tick_test.go` 175, `world/export_test.go` 9, `session/overmind_radius_test.go` 16, `world/overmind_txguard.go`, `world/overmind_txguard_test.go`, `session/overmind_skin.go`). Every addition is marked "Overmind fork".

Nothing else differs from upstream. When pulling a new upstream version, copy it over this folder, reapply these and see whether `Player` calls any new session method (the compiler will say).

## Known upstream issues left alone

A very large edit made with the default `SetOpts` freezes the world for seconds: each `SetBlock` queues redstone and neighbour updates, and the next tick works through all of them (`redstoneEngine.compile`, `performNeighbourUpdates`). About 920 000 calls cost about 8 s and stalled every player's tick. Overmind's tests pass `DisableBlockUpdates` and `DisableRedstoneUpdates` for bulk fills. It is upstream behaviour and a known risk for big explosions and fills; nothing is changed for now.
